checks.label: The domain includes all real inputs that would not cause an undefined operation, such as dividing by zero or taking the square root of a negative number: dragged along the one-over, the beam finds no value at 0 and a value at every other input; along the root, no value at every negative input and a value from 0 up

The range is the set of y values for a given domain: for every setting of the ends on the line, the square and the flow meter, the output shadow runs from the lowest to the highest output on the curve between them, and with inputs from −2 to 3 the square's runs 0 to 9, not 4 to 9

Instruments convert with the linear equation y = mx + b, a straight line: S(p) = 0.16p + 4 rises 0.16 mA for every 1%, gives 4 mA at 0% and 20 mA at 100%, and the transmitter's shadows read 0% to 100% and 4 mA to 20 mA
The root of a number from 0 to 1 is larger, √0.5 = 0.707, so a 12 mA signal from the DP cell is 50% DP but 71% flow rate: S(50) = 12 mA, and the flow meter's beam up from 0.5 reads 0.707

The pressure difference is proportional to the square of the flow, so flow is scaled from the square root of the pressure difference: every flow on the meter's curve, squared, gives back its pressure difference, and both its shadows run 0 to 1

Every worked number is right: S(25) = 8, S(75) = 16, S(50) = 12 and S(100) = 20 mA; the square gives 9 for −3 and 3, 4 for −2 and 0 for 0; 1/−1 = −1, 1/0.01 = 100, 1/−4 = −0.25 and 1/4 = 0.25; √0 = 0, √4 = 2 and √9 = 3; 12 V draws 4 A through 3 Ω and 1 A through 12 Ω; the hump is 2 high at −4 and 4 and 6 high at 0

A vertical asymptote is a vertical line that the graph approaches but never crosses: as the one-over's input nears 0 its output passes any height, up on the right and down on the left, the curve is drawn on both sides of the dashed line x = 0 and never on it

A horizontal asymptote is a horizontal line that the graph approaches as the input increases or decreases without bound: far out the one-over's output shrinks towards 0 and never reaches it, and the beam dragged out to 4 reads 0.25 beside the dashed line y = 0

The poles are the values where the denominator is equal to zero, the points where the function is not defined: the one-over's denominator is x, so its one pole is 0, where the beam finds no value, while just either side it finds one
Before Check a puzzle draws no answer; the right answer draws its shadow or reading and nothing in red, and each wrong answer draws its own slip in red

The picture tells the truth: every dot on a graph sits on its curve at its place; the one-over's two shadows run on at both ends with a hole at 0; the root's both start with a filled dot at 0 and run on; and every shadow set by two ends ends in two filled dots
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3.4 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
